Inside the Little Italy Patisserie Turning San Diego Onto French Pastry, One Custom Cake at a Time

By There San Diego Staff · San Diego

Tucked into a corner unit at 320 W Cedar St, Bonjour Patisserie has quietly become the place San Diegans go when a birthday, a wedding, or just a Tuesday calls for something better than a grocery-store bakery case. This is an online bakery and patisserie shop built around French desserts and pastries, and it treats the category with the kind of seriousness usually reserved for restaurants with tasting menus, not cake counters.

A Case Built on Precision, Not Volume

Where a lot of bakeries try to be everything to everyone, Bonjour Patisserie has kept its focus narrow and its execution tight. The offering is a curated selection of desserts and pastries rather than a sprawling menu, which is exactly the point. French patisserie rewards restraint. A croissant either laminates properly or it doesn't, and a mousse cake either holds its structure or it collapses under its own ambition. The shop's reputation, reflected in a 4.7-star rating across 429 reviews, suggests a kitchen that has chosen to do fewer things and do them precisely.

The Cakes Are Where the Ambition Shows

Ask around and the conversation eventually turns to the cakes. Bonjour Patisserie builds large custom cakes for order, and has developed a specific niche in wedding cakes for couples planning their day in San Diego. That's a different discipline from a display case of croissants. It means consultations, structural engineering under fondant or buttercream, and delivery logistics for something that has to survive a car ride and still look photograph-ready at 4pm on someone's biggest day of the year. That the business handles both the everyday pastry counter and this higher-stakes cake work speaks to a kitchen comfortable operating at more than one register.

An online bakery and patisserie shop specializing in French desserts and pastries, offering a curated selection of desserts, pastries, and large custom cakes for order and delivery.

The desserts themselves lean into what French pastry does that American baking often skips: layered textures, restrained sweetness, and finishing work that looks intentional rather than decorative for its own sake. It's the kind of case where you order one thing to eat in the car and one thing to bring home, and both survive the drive better than they have any right to.

First Visit? Here's the Move

Because the ordering happens ahead of the visit, especially for anything cake-sized, the smart approach is to browse first. Start on bonjourpatisserie.com, get a sense of the current pastry selection and cake styles, and place an order for pickup or delivery around the occasion you're planning for, whether that's a wedding, a birthday, or a dessert table that needs to punch above its weight. For custom and wedding cake work especially, giving the kitchen lead time pays off in exactly the kind of detail that makes a cake memorable rather than just serviceable.

For a shop doing this level of pastry and cake work out of a single Cedar Street address, the next step is simple: place the order before the occasion sneaks up on you.
